definition: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, made up of right and left hemispheres, each with an outer cerebral cortex and deeper basal ganglia. It includes most brain structures inside the skull except the medulla oblongata, pons, and cerebellum, and it supports movement and sensation as well as emotional and intellectual functions.
